title: VYREX — Investigation orchestrator
description: Health and behaviour of the LangGraph investigation orchestrator. Reads Postgres directly rather than Prometheus: the orchestrator is a poll loop with no HTTP surface, so adding a /metrics endpoint would mean adding a web server to a service that deliberately has none. The state that matters is already durable in the orchestration tables.

panels.title: Queue depth (unclaimed)
panels.description: Outbox rows still pending. Sustained non-zero with a running orchestrator means it is stuck, not busy — investigations are serial by design (ORCH_CONCURRENCY=1), so a small backlog is normal.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS "pending" FROM investigation_outbox WHERE status <> 'sent';

panels.title: Oldest pending (minutes)
panels.description: Age of the oldest unclaimed job. More diagnostic than queue depth: a depth of 1 that never clears is a wedged worker.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - min(created_at))) / 60, 0) AS "oldest_min" FROM investigation_outbox WHERE status <> 'sent';

panels.title: Run outcomes
panels.description: 'partial' is not a failure: it means the graph finished with at least one branch skipped or failed, which is the designed degraded path. 'failed' is the one to alert on.

targets.rawSql: SELECT status AS "metric", count(*) AS "value" FROM investigations GROUP BY status ORDER BY 2 DESC;

panels.title: Verdicts carrying ≥1 citation
panels.description: THE grounding metric, and the Phase 2 exit gate. A non-abstaining verdict with no cited claim is rejected by the contract, so this counts verdicts that actually committed AND grounded. Measured at 0 for llama3.2:3b and qwen2.5:3b across 12 findings each — see docs/AGENT-ORCHESTRATION.md §7.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE jsonb_array_length(COALESCE(rationale_claims, '[]'::jsonb)) > 0) AS "cited", count(*) AS "total" FROM triage_reports;

panels.title: Synthesis latency (LLM step, seconds)
panels.description: The dominant cost. Everything else in the graph is deterministic SQL measured in milliseconds.

targets.rawSql: SELECT finished_at AS "time", duration_ms / 1000.0 AS "synthesis_s" FROM investigation_steps WHERE node = 'synthesize' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(finished_at) ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Node duration (median ms, log scale)
panels.description: Log scale on purpose: synthesis is ~1000x the specialists, so a linear axis renders every deterministic node as a flat line at zero and hides the one thing this panel is for — showing that only one node is slow, and it is the only one that calls a model.

targets.rawSql: SELECT node, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY duration_ms) AS "p50_ms" FROM investigation_steps WHERE duration_ms IS NOT NULL GROUP BY node ORDER BY 2 DESC;

panels.title: Branch health — succeeded / skipped / failed per node
panels.description: Skipped and failed are DIFFERENT facts and are kept apart deliberately: 'found nothing' and 'crashed' look identical in a single-blob agent, and an analyst has to be able to tell them apart. A node that starts failing is usually a missing DB grant — see tests/test_db_grants.py.

targets.rawSql: SELECT node, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'succeeded') AS "ok", count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'skipped') AS "skipped", count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') AS "failed", max(reason) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') AS "last failure reason" FROM investigation_steps GROUP BY node ORDER BY 4 DESC, 1;

panels.title: Recent verdicts
panels.description: model_name is shown because it is the first thing to check before comparing two runs: a fake-llm run and a real one are not comparable, and forgetting that produced a wrong conclusion once already.

targets.rawSql: SELECT i.created_at AS "when", i.subject_id AS "finding", i.model_name AS "model", r.recommended_disposition AS "verdict", r.confidence, jsonb_array_length(COALESCE(r.rationale_claims, '[]'::jsonb)) AS "claims", (SELECT count(*) FROM investigation_evidence e WHERE e.investigation_id = i.investigation_id) AS "evidence" FROM investigations i LEFT JOIN triage_reports r USING (investigation_id) ORDER BY i.created_at DESC LIMIT 25;
